# Vea — canonical monorepo (contracts + validator + relayer)

Canonical implementation of **Vea**, a trust-minimized, optimistically-verified
cross-chain message bridge (Kleros). This repo holds the Solidity contracts and
the official **TypeScript** bots.

- `contracts/` — Solidity (Hardhat). The protocol truth.
- `validator-cli/` — `@kleros/vea-validator-cli`: Oracle + Challenger
  (saveSnapshot, claim, challenge, startVerification, verifySnapshot, withdraw).
- `relayer-cli/` — `@kleros/vea-relayer-cli`: relays messages for verified roots
  (+ Hashi helpers).

## Toolchain

Node 22+, Yarn Berry 4.6.0 (`corepack enable` if `yarn` is missing), workspaces,
`nodeLinker: node-modules`. `contracts/typechain-types/` and artifacts are
**generated** (gitignored) — build contracts before using the CLIs.

```bash
yarn install
yarn workspace @kleros/vea-contracts build            # generates typechain-types
yarn workspace @kleros/vea-validator-cli test         # jest, offline (mocked)
yarn workspace @kleros/vea-relayer-cli test           # jest, offline
yarn workspace <pkg> exec tsc --noEmit
```

## Safety (non-negotiable)

- **No live chain in this repo by default.** `yarn start` / `yarn start-relayer`
  and any claim/challenge/saveSnapshot/relay against a real network are only ever
  run by a human with a funded `.env`. Deposits are real value even on testnet.
- **Never commit or print `.env*` files or private keys.**
- **Never conflate the three chains.** Arbitrum Sepolia `421614` (inbox),
  Sepolia `11155111` (outbox/arbToEth + router/arbToGnosis), Chiado `10200`
  (outbox/arbToGnosis). Block numbers/tags are per-chain.
- **Dual ethers:** v5 (`@ethersproject/providers`, Arbitrum SDK) and v6
  (`ethers`, typechain) are used together — keep them straight at each call site.

## Protocol invariants (quick reference)

- Epoch = `block.timestamp / epochPeriod`.
- `Claim` is **never stored on-chain**, only `claimHashes[epoch] =
  keccak256(abi.encodePacked(stateRoot, claimer, uint32 tsClaimed, uint32
  tsVerification, uint32 blockVerification, uint8 honest, address challenger))`.
  State-changing calls need the exact preimage or they revert `"Invalid claim."`.
- Verdicts only from immutable inbox reads: `finalized` L2 tag past epoch end,
  or `latest` only after `sequencerDelayLimit` past epoch end.
- Winner of a dispute takes `1.5 × deposit`; half the loser's burns.

See `validator-cli/README.md`, `relayer-cli/README.md`, and the Solidity under
`contracts/src/` for details. `AGENTS.md` at the workspace root
(`/home/agentops/dev/vea_validators/AGENTS.md`) is the master cross-repo info
file.

name: {{short-kebab-case-slug}}
description: {{one-line summary, used to decide relevance in future conversations, so be specific}}
metadata:

- If the memory names a file path: check the file exists.
- If the memory names a function or flag: grep for it.

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

# This Action will scan dependency manifest files that change as part of a Pull Request,
# surfacing known-vulnerable versions of the packages declared or updated in the PR.
# Once installed, if the workflow run is marked as required,
# PRs introducing known-vulnerable packages will be blocked from merging.
#

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GHSA exception policy (read before touching `allow-ghsas` below)

#      unreviewed.

#   * every id in `allow-ghsas` has an exception block in this file;

#     yarn.lock resolves, so a version bump that fixes the vulnerability forces
#     a human back into this file.
